Overview

The Databricks Campus Hackathon – RVCE Edition is a 12-hour AI hackathon hosted by Buildora in collaboration with Databricks as part of Bengaluru Tech Week 2026.

The hackathon brings together students interested in AI, software development, product building, and problem-solving to work in teams, build innovative solutions, and solve real-world challenges using modern technologies.

Students from any college or university are eligible to participate. Anyone with an interest in AI, software development, product building, and emerging technologies is encouraged to take part.

HACKATHON HIGHLIGHTS

  • Build solutions during an intensive 12-hour AI hackathon.
  • Collaborate with fellow student builders and innovators.
  • Explore and build using Databricks technologies.
  • Solve real-world problems through AI and technology.
  • Learn, experiment, and build alongside other developers.
  • Showcase your solution to an expert jury.

SELECTION PROCESS

Each participating campus will host its own 12-hour hackathon.

The top 5 teams will qualify for the Grand Finale at BMS College of Engineering, Bengaluru, where finalists will present their solutions before an expert jury.

GRAND FINALE

The selected teams from BMSCE and RVCE Edition will compete at the Grand Finale at BMS College of Engineering, Bengaluru.

Three winning teams will be selected during the Grand Finale and compete for a combined ₹1,00,000 prize pool, sponsored by Logitech.

IMPORTANT INFORMATION

Every participant must sign up for Databricks Free Edition before attending the hackathon.

Problem statements will be announced soon. Stay tuned for further updates and get ready to build, innovate, and solve real-world challenges.

Build with Databricks. Build for the Real World.

Themes

Track A: Real-World Campus Problem Solver

Build an application that solves a practical problem for students, educators, researchers, administrators, placement teams, clubs, or campus operations teams . Possible directions include: • Placement and skills-readiness insights • Academic resource discovery • Research and publication exploration • Campus sustainability and energy monitoring • Transport and mobility planning • Facility or laboratory utilisation • Student-club and event engagement • Resource allocation and operational planning • Accessibility, safety, or student-support discovery Focus on usefulness, a clearly defined user, and a complete journey from question to data-backed answer . The solution must use Databricks Free Edition , with a Genie Agent at its core . Genie must meaningfully power the product's central experience.

Genie-Powered Campus IntelligenceRead more

Track B: Creative Campus Intelligence

Create an original or unexpected way for people to explore, understand, or experience campus life using real, open, or responsibly generated synthetic data. Possible directions include: • A campus culture or community explorer • A research-connections discovery engine • A student opportunity navigator • A conversational campus history experience • A data-powered “what if?” simulator • An intelligent campus recommendation experience • An unexpected application combining campus and public city data Originality matters , but Genie must still play an essential role in the experience. The solution must use Databricks Free Edition , with a Genie Agent at its core .

Eligibility

Profile Type:
Students

  • Participants must register through the hackathon platform before the registration deadline.
  • Teams must consist of 3 to 5 members.
  • Each participant can be part of only one team.

  • The BMSCE edition is an offline hackathon held at BMS College of Engineering, Bengaluru.

Rules

Team Formation

  • Teams must consist of 3 to 5 members.
  • Each participant can be part of only one team.
  • Teams must complete their registration and team formation before the deadline.

Project Development

  • Teams must develop their solutions during the official hackathon.
  • Participants are expected to use Databricks technologies as part of their solution.
  • All submitted work must be original.

Submission

  • Teams must submit all required project deliverables before the submission deadline.
  • Late submissions may not be considered for evaluation.
  • Further submission requirements will be communicated by the organizers.

Judging & Selection

  • The top 5 teams from this Edition will qualify for the Grand Finale at BMS College of Engineering, Bengaluru.
  • Shortlisting will be based on the submitted team profiles.
  • Finalist teams will present their solutions before an expert jury.
  • The decision of the judging panel will be final.

Code of Conduct

  • Participants must maintain professional and respectful conduct throughout the hackathon.
  • Plagiarism, cheating, or misrepresentation of work is not permitted.
  • Any violation of the event rules may result in disqualification.

General

  • Participants must complete the required Databricks Free Edition signup before attending.
  • Participants must follow all instructions and deadlines communicated by the organizers.
  • Organizers reserve the right to make necessary changes to the event schedule or rules.
